subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get a first-class hard tool policy, and should that be a new `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` layer or documented inheritance from `tools.subagents.tools`?
rationale: The choice defines a public config surface and authorization boundary for unattended scheduled runs, including precedence against existing policy layers, per-job `payload.toolsAllow`, and message delivery behavior.

options.title: Design Cron Policy In Session Model
options.body: Recommended: define one canonical cron/session policy path first, then implement cron enforcement with docs and tests across delivery modes.

options.title: Add Dedicated Cron Scope Now
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.*` as a narrow global cron policy with explicit deny precedence over per-job allowlists and documented upgrade behavior.

options.title: Rely On Per-Job Tools Only
options.body: Decline a global cron policy and document per-job `toolsAllow` plus current delivery safeguards as the supported workflow.

recommendation.title: Design Cron Policy In Session Model
recommendation.body: Recommended: define one canonical cron/session policy path first, then implement cron enforcement with docs and tests across delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has already reviewed this exact issue and is the strongest visible routing candidate for the config/security-boundary decision.
